identity.title: Severe postural dizziness / inability to stand for vitals

technique.how: After supine vitals, stand the patient (with assistance) and ask about dizziness while measuring pulse and BP at about 1 minute. 'Severe' means dizziness so marked the patient cannot stay standing long enough for upright vitals or nearly faints; record it as a positive finding in its own right, together with any pulse increment of 30/min or more.
technique.prerequisites: Supine rest for at least 2 minutes before standing; an assistant to prevent a fall. Sitting is not an adequate substitute for standing.
technique.contraindications: Do not stand a patient who is already hypotensive, in shock, or with suspected unstable spine/pelvic injury.

interpretation.positive_finding: Severe postural dizziness (or a postural pulse increment >=30/min) is highly specific (0.98) for hypovolaemia from blood loss and is present in almost all subjects after large (630-1150 mL) blood loss.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence is reassuring only against large blood loss (sensitivity 0.97); after moderate (450-630 mL) loss the finding is usually absent (sensitivity 0.22), so a negative test does not exclude clinically important haemorrhage.
interpretation.pitfalls: Mild postural dizziness has no proven diagnostic value; supine tachycardia or hypotension is often absent even after 1 L loss. Evidence comes from healthy volunteers after phlebotomy, not from elderly or medicated ED patients, in whom baseline orthostatic symptoms are common.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: treat as significant volume loss - IV access, fluid/blood, search for bleeding source; negative: does not exclude moderate haemorrhage, use labs/other findings.

estimates.target_condition: Hypovolaemia from LARGE acute blood loss (630-1150 mL) - finding: severe postural dizziness (preventing upright vitals) OR postural pulse increment >=30/min
estimates.population: Healthy adult volunteers undergoing phlebotomy (pooled RCE analysis of postural vital-sign studies)
estimates.reference_standard: Known volume of blood removed by phlebotomy (before vs after)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.97/(1-0.98) = 48.5; LR- = (1-0.97)/0.98 = 0.03; from abstract sensitivity 97% and specificity 98%
estimates.quote: a much greater sensitivity for large blood loss of 97% (95% CI, 91%-100%); the corresponding specificity is 98% (95% CI, 97%-99%)

estimates.target_condition: Hypovolaemia from MODERATE acute blood loss (450-630 mL) - finding: severe postural dizziness OR postural pulse increment >=30/min
estimates.population: Healthy adult volunteers undergoing phlebotomy (pooled RCE analysis of postural vital-sign studies)
estimates.reference_standard: Known volume of blood removed by phlebotomy (before vs after)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.22/(1-0.98) = 11; LR- = (1-0.22)/0.98 = 0.80; specificity 98% is the single value reported for the finding in the abstract
estimates.quote: The presence of either finding has a sensitivity for moderate blood loss of only 22% (95% confidence interval [CI], 6%-48%)

sources.citation: McGee S, Abernethy WB 3rd, Simel DL. The rational clinical examination. Is this patient hypovolemic? JAMA. 1999;281(11):1022-1029.
Witting MD, Wears RL, Li S. Defining the positive tilt test: a study of healthy adults with moderate acute blood loss. Ann Emerg Med. 1994;23(6):1320-1323.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not attempt standing in patients who are hypotensive supine, obtunded, or at high fall risk; do not apply the volunteer-derived numbers uncritically to elderly patients on antihypertensives, beta-blockers or with autonomic neuropathy.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Inability to stand because of dizziness in a patient with suspected bleeding indicates large-volume loss: obtain large-bore access, type and crossmatch, and escalate immediately.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: The RCE combines severe dizziness with the pulse-increment criterion; 'severe' is defined operationally (unable to complete upright vitals), which limits subjectivity. Mild dizziness is not a positive finding.

extraction_notes: Numbers are verbatim from the McGee 1999 RCE abstract (not open access; tables not viewable), which reports the COMBINED finding 'severe postural dizziness (preventing measurement of upright vital signs) or a postural pulse increment of 30 beats/min or more' - the two components are not separated in the abstract, so the estimate is for the composite. Specificity 98% (97-99) is reported once and applied to both blood-loss strata as in the abstract; LRs are computed from sens/spec (computed=true). The abstract states 'The finding of mild postural dizziness has no proven value' - recorded in pitfalls. Witting 1994 (PMID 8198307, 345 blood donors, 450 mL phlebotomy) is the principal primary study behind the moderate-loss estimate; its abstract gives no numeric sensitivity/specificity, so no estimate is attributed to it. Population is healthy volunteers, not ED patients with vomiting/diarrhoea; for that group the RCE found postural findings of unproven utility.
